title: soft-reservation-band-controller-and-adaptive-warmup-governor
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce soft reservation bands to provide deterministic minimum throughput guarantees for Dedicated fleets, plus an adaptive warmup governor to reduce headroom waste during scale-ups. Includes telemetry for per-tenant reservation utilization and warmup effectiveness.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets sometimes over-provision headroom to guard against transient bursts, which increases unit costs. Conversely, aggressive scale-up without a controlled warmup period causes downstream cold-start latency. This change introduces a soft reservation band controller (SRB) that enforces a contracted minimum throughput band while allowing opportunistic utilization above the band, and an Adaptive Warmup Governor (AWG) that ramps reserved capacity in measured steps using observed utilization and request latency signals.

What this PR does (single string): Adds an SRB controller that maintains per-tenant 'soft' reservation bands with a configurable lower and upper bound, implements a conservative escalation policy for reservation increases, and a decay policy for reservation reduction. The AWG coordinates warm-pool activation and gradual instance readiness windows to smooth KV-cache warming and model shard loading. The controller emits new telemetry (reservation_band_{min,max}, reservation_inflight_adjust, warmup_ramp_pct) and augments existing utilization sampling with warmup-aware histograms so SLO calculations can exclude transient warmup noise.

Design highlights: - Soft reservation bands are stored as reservation leases with stamps to allow eventual consistency across controller replicas. - Reservation changes are enacted using a two-phase commit: plan (dry-run metrics + predicted latency) then enact (graceful drain/provision). - AWG uses a PID-inspired controller tuned per-pool class (interactive/batch) and a backoff table for hostile environments (preemption/spot churn). - We avoid hard reclaims during warmup; instead the system places ephemeral soft credits that can be reclaimed preemptively if cluster pressure is high. - Telemetry hooks are lightweight: a stamped sample every 5s, and a warmup-aware utilization sample every 10s; metrics are labeled by tenant_id, pool_class, and rollout_tag.

Commits (high-level): [1] introduce SRB CRD and controller scaffolding; [2] implement band reconciliation and lease manager; [3] AWG: ramp algorithm + warm-pool hooks; [4] telemetry: metrics + dashboards + unit tests; [5] integration tests for scale-up/down scenarios; [6] docs and upgrade notes.

Files changed (high level): - controllers/srb/controller.go (band reconciliation, lease logic) - controllers/srb/lease_manager.go (lease stamp & conflict resolution) - controllers/awg/driver.go (ramp algorithm) - controllers/awg/hooks.go (warm-pool activation) - pkg/telemetry/warmup_sampler.go (sampling + histograms) - charts/dedicated/templates/srb-config.yaml (defaults + feature flag) - docs/operations/dedicated-reservation-bands.md (operator guide) - tests/integration/srb_warmup_test.go (end-to-end scenarios)

Small illustrative snippet (controller decision logic): "if observed_utilization < band.min*0.85 and sustained(60s) then schedule_decay(steps=band.min*0.1) else if latency_sla_breached and headroom_ok then plan_increase(steps=calc_step())".

Review conversation (timeline condensed): - Arjun (2026-02-12): "High-level looks solid. Concern: two-phase enact needs clear rollback semantics if provision fails mid-drain. Please add a circuit that cancels enact if >10% of requests see degraded latency during enact window." - Maya (2026-02-13): "Added enact circuit and a non-blocking fallback to a compatible model variant. Updated tests to simulate enact failure." - Lukas (2026-02-16): "Please document interaction with existing burst-token pool and explain allowed invariants when soft credits are reclaimed." - Maya (2026-02-18): "Expanded docs and added a utility to reconcile burst-token metadata when SRB reclaims credits." - Sofia (2026-02-20): "CI showed a flaky test in awg_ramp_test; please stabilize by increasing timing slack and adding deterministic clock in unit tests." - Maya (2026-02-21): "Stabilized tests with fake clock, reduced integration timeouts, and reran CI." - Arjun (2026-02-24): "LGTM after one minor comment about telemetry tag cardinality." - Arjun (2026-02-25): "Approved and applied squash merge."

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass (one rerun for awg_ramp_test due to timing; stabilized) - linters: pass - benchmark-lab/sim: pass on staging (p95 latency improved during measured warmups; cost delta -4% on typical desktop workload). Notes: a single synthetic test in perf-canary timed out in a spotty region; we gated the canary and left a follow-up (ENG-1863) to repro.

Backward compatibility & upgrade notes: - SRB feature is off by default; operators must enable charts/dedicated/templates/srb-config.yaml and set featureFlag.srb=true. - Existing reservation semantics remain unchanged until an operator opts into SRB. - Telemetry metric names are additive; no breaking metrics renames. - There is a small control-plane schema migration to add a lease_stamp field; migration is idempotent and documented in docs/operations/dedicated-reservation-bands.md.

Operational playbook (short): - To enable: flip feature flag, monitor reservation_band_min and reservation_band_max for sudden gaps. - If runaway increases observed: set global_max_reservation_pct to cap. - If warmup latency spikes: reduce warmup_ramp_pct or increase warm-pool size for that pool_class.

Follow-ups: - ENG-1863: investigate perf-canary timeout root cause in us-west-2 spot pool. - ENG-1899: add per-tenant warmup-eval checks to Redwood Optimize suggestions. - SRE-78: add alerting for repeated SRB-enact failures (5x in 10m).
